Title: TLS SNI auto_sni Assertion Crash / Connection Failure via Long Downstream Request Authority (CVE-2024-32475)
Analysis:
Trace:
- **Source**: Untrusted user downstream HTTP request `:authority` header (or host) of length > 255.
- **Sanitization/Validation**: There is no validation of the SNI length to be strictly within BoringSSL's limits (<= 255 characters) in either `source/common/router/router.cc` or `Http::Utility::parseAuthority()`.
- **Sink**: `SSL_set_tlsext_host_name` called in `source/common/tls/context_impl.cc` at line 717. When the `:authority` is > 255 characters, BoringSSL enforces the standard limit and returns 0 (failure). In unpatched Envoy versions, this triggered a `RELEASE_ASSERT` causing a crash. In newer versions, it returns `absl::InvalidArgumentError` causing upstream connection failure/termination.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
A downstream request with an `:authority` header containing 256 or more characters, targeting a cluster configured with `auto_sni: true` and upstream TLS.

```http
GET / HTTP/1.1
Host: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa.example.com
Connection: keep-alive
```
This hostname has more than 255 characters, causing BoringSSL's hostname setter to fail.

Title: Integer Overflow leading to Infinite Loop in RDB Set Loading (RDB_TYPE_SET)
Analysis:
An integer overflow vulnerability exists in `src/rdb.c` inside the `rdbLoadObject` function when parsing sets of type `RDB_TYPE_SET`.

### Source
The vulnerability is triggered when loading an RDB file containing a set data structure. The length of the set is loaded into a 64-bit unsigned integer (`len`) using `rdbLoadLen(rdb, NULL)` at line 1873.

### Sanitization/Validation
There is no validation check to ensure that the 64-bit length `len` fits within the range of a 32-bit unsigned integer before it is used as a loop boundary.

### Sink
At line 1894, a loop is executed to load every member of the set:
```c
        for (i = 0; i < len; i++) {
```
The loop counter `i` is declared as an `unsigned int` (which is 32-bit on almost all modern platforms) at line 1828, whereas `len` is `uint64_t`. If a maliciously crafted RDB file provides a set length `len` greater than `UINT_MAX` (e.g., `4294967296`), the 32-bit loop counter `i` will increment up to `4294967295`, and then wrap around back to `0`. Since `0 < 4294967296` is true, the condition `i < len` remains perpetually satisfied, causing an infinite loop. This blocks the main thread, resulting in a severe Denial of Service (DoS) vulnerability.

### Conceptual Exploit Payload
A sample RDB file prefixing a Set key with a length encoding of `0x83` or `0x82` followed by a large 64-bit integer length (e.g., `0x0000000100000000` / `4294967296`). When parsed, `len` will be decoded as `4294967296`. The server will attempt to parse set members, but the loop counter `i` will overflow and run infinitely.
VulnType: CWE-835: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop')
